item.title: Contemplative Citizenship — Tue Oct 13, 7:00 PM — Saint James Chapel and Zoom
item.description:
Contemplative Citizenship: Lord, make me an instrument of your peace. October 13 – November 10 7 – 8:00 PM in the Chapel In person and via Zoom This Fall, our worship and teaching will be guided by a single line from the Prayer of Saint Francis: “Lord, make me an instrument of your peace.” We will begin this initiative at our Saturday Night Mass on October 3, with local musician and pastor Liz Fulmer leading music that inspires us to embody God’s peace in our lives. On Tuesday, October 13, we will start a 5-week Fall Contemplative Citizenship series in which we will reflect on various lines from the prayer, exploring what it means to embody this prayer in both our personal lives and in our civic responsibilities, especially during this election season when our country feels divided and stressed.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Evening Compline — Tue Oct 13, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: PDF@Zoetropolis Presents Get Out — Thu Oct 15, 6:30 PM — Zoetropolis Cinema Stillhouse
item.description:
October brings horror to PDF at Zoetropolis with Jordan Peele’s acclaimed Get Out. What begins as an awkward weekend visit to the family of Chris’s white girlfriend gradually becomes a distinctly American nightmare. Blending horror, satire, mystery, and comedy, Peele turns familiar genre conventions inside out while exploring race, liberal self-congratulation, bodily autonomy, and the difference between being noticed and being recognized as a person.
Our Halloween-month screening opens the final sequence of the yearlong America 250 film series, Reckoning & Futurity: What Are We Still Fighting For? As the series moves toward its conclusion, Get Out asks whether America’s history of racial domination has disappeared or simply assumed more polite and apparently inclusive forms.

item.title: Pre-Prohibition Study Hall — Thu Oct 15, 6:30 PM — The Conway Room
item.description:
Before Prohibition, there was the cocktail.
Step back into the earliest days of American cocktail culture at The Conway Room for an evening exploring the drinks, techniques, and traditions that shaped the American bar. This Study Hall will take you behind the recipes and rituals of pre-Prohibition drinking culture, with a curated selection of historic cocktails, classic techniques, and stories from the early days of American bartending. You’ll have the chance to taste your way through cocktail history, learn how these early drinks were crafted, and get hands-on by building a cocktail of your own. The evening will also feature a selection of refined, tavern-inspired canapés, including smoked trout deviled eggs and tea sandwiches with smoked salmon, cucumber, lemon and dill, alongside other classic bites to enjoy throughout the experience. item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Fri Oct 9, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.description:
Born in Philadelphia, raised in Middletown, and educated in Lancaster County, W. Miller Barbour carried the lessons of his Pennsylvania upbringing onto a national stage. A pioneering African American human rights advocate, Barbour challenged discrimination in housing, employment, education, and civic life. Although he became an important figure in the struggle for racial equality, his remarkable life and achievements have largely faded from public memory.
The Historic Preservation Trust of Lancaster County invites you to rediscover his story during the next presentation in our 2026 Speaker Series, “W. Miller Barbour: Lancaster County Legacy,” presented by public historian Eric Schubert. Barbour’s life connected Lancaster County to a much broader movement for equality and justice in 20th-century America. Winnie-the-Pooh is celebrating its 100th birthday this year! The stories A.A. Milne created have become classics that are as beloved now as they were when they were first published in October 1926. In celebration of the centennial of Milne’s timeless tales, join Dr. Sarah Jackson, Assistant Professor from the Department of Early, Middle, and Elementary Education at Millersville University to learn about how these beloved children’s stories have endured as they have been translated and adapted countless times since their publication 100 years ago. Dr. Jackson will focus on the influence of colonialism in the stories and consider how the animal characters try on—and resist—colonial language. All ages welcome, but this will be a lecture-style program geared toward the young at heart

Church of the Apostles and the American Cancer Society Relay for Life are teaming up for a festive morning of Breakfast with Santa and a Holiday Bazaar on Saturday, December 12! We’re making this year’s event bigger and better, with kids’ crafts and fun games provided by COA while parents browse a variety of local vendors throughout Fellowship Hall and our West Wing Lobby. And, of course, Santa will make his grand arrival by fire truck at 9 AM! 🚒🎅 Doors open at 8:45 AM. Breakfast will be served by wonderful American Cancer Society volunteers from 9–11 AM, with photos with Santa, crafts, raffles, and the Holiday Bazaar continuing until noon. Breakfast: • Adults and ages 13+: $12 • Children ages 2–12: $7 • Children under 2: Free The Holiday Bazaar is free to attend, and breakfast proceeds benefit the American Cancer Society Relay for Life of Lancaster County. Come hungry, bring the kids, and get your holiday season started with a morning of food, fun, shopping, and Santa! 🎄
